reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises for Al0.5CoCrFeNi. E1 discusses general HEA strengthening mechanisms without mentioning precipitates or aging. E2 addresses corrosion resistance in a different alloy (Cantor alloy) via grain growth, not nanoprecipitates. E3 describes precipitation strengthening in refractory HEAs with different compositions and precipitate types (sigma phase), not coherent nanoprecipitates in Al0.5CoCrFeNi. None of the evidence supports the claimed diffusion barrier mechanism for oxidation/corrosion.
premises: Aging Al0.5CoCrFeNi at 500–600 °C forms nanoscale coherent precipitates
These precipitates hinder dislocation motion, increasing yield strength
These precipitates act as diffusion barriers, improving corrosion and oxidation resistance
Precipitate coarsening or dissolution above ~700 °C eliminates these benefits
The cited evidence supports these mechanisms in related alloy systems
